description: A director of undergraduate research must authorize a student-led survey of first-year students and finalize the survey's collection settings, consent process, data retention, enrollment scope, and presentation rules, with input from the research coordinator, institutional privacy officer, and faculty mentor.

shared_context.S1: A student research team has proposed an online survey of first-year students about their transition to college.
shared_context.S2: The draft proposal describes an anonymous survey, indefinite retention of responses, an open invitation to all first-year students, and eligibility for a public research presentation.
shared_context.S3: Dr. Holt must give the final authorization and record the operating conditions before the survey can launch.
shared_context.S4: The undergraduate research office routinely holds a pre-authorization review in which the research coordinator, privacy officer, and faculty mentor report any conditions that should be included.

PF1.text: Mr. Grant tested the survey platform and confirmed that it collects respondent email addresses by default; the launch settings must disable email collection and delete the existing test responses before student data are gathered. He recorded this in the platform test log, which is kept separate from the draft proposal.

PF2.text: Ms. Shah's policy review found that the survey includes questions about mental-health treatment and immigration status, which are classified as sensitive student data; the project therefore requires explicit written consent, encrypted institutional storage, and deletion of research responses exactly 30 days after collection closes. She entered the determination in the privacy review system, which is separate from the research proposal.

PF3.text: Dr. Brooks confirmed that the course attached to this project awards credit only for a study capped at exactly 100 enrolled respondents and permits dissemination only at the closed university undergraduate symposium, not at a public presentation. She placed these course conditions in the faculty mentoring record, which has not yet been attached to the proposal.

acceptance_conditions: The survey must be authorized with email collection disabled.
All existing platform test responses must be deleted before launch.
Explicit written consent must be required.
Responses must be stored in encrypted institutional storage.
Research responses must be deleted exactly 30 days after collection closes.
Enrollment must be capped at exactly 100 respondents.
The presentation must be limited to the closed university undergraduate symposium.
A formal privacy implementation commitment must be recorded.
A formal research-platform cleanup commitment must be recorded.
A formal course-condition implementation commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The platform test confirms that email collection is active and that test responses exist, changing the launch setting to disabled, the cleanup decision to true, and the required cleanup commitment.
The privacy classification changes the plan from anonymous ordinary handling to written consent, encrypted institutional storage, and deletion exactly 30 days after collection closes.
The course conditions change the respondent limit to exactly 100, restrict dissemination to the closed university undergraduate symposium, and require a course-condition implementation commitment.
